The sizes are in µm and the shapes (cordate, obovate, concave) belong to the bracts around a bryophyte's archegonia, so this is not the angiosperm involucre PO_0009100, which is defined for clusters of flowers. In a liverwort flora the female involucre is the perichaetial sheath or bracts. If the flora turns out to be about hornworts or thalloid Marchantiales, a separate class would be needed. Check the source flora before adding this rule.

label: underleaf
definition: A non-vascular leaf (PO:0025075) of a leafy liverwort that is inserted on the ventral side of the stem, in a third row distinct from the two lateral rows of leaves, and is usually smaller than the lateral leaves and differently shaped.
reason: A standard structure in every treatment of leafy liverworts (described as bilobed, distant or absent). PO has non-vascular leaf but nothing for the ventral row. 'Ventral' is not a series-position context word, so the patterns can't express it. Propose to PO upstream as a child of non-vascular leaf.

Narrower. A single conic, flattened, entire, caducous structure between the petioles of opposite leaves is an interpetiolar stipule (or the stipular sheath's appendage), e.g. in Rubiaceae. The qualities fit a stipule.

label: cyathial gland appendage
parent: is_a PO_0025496 (multi-tissue plant structure); part_of PO_0009035 (nectary)
definition: A multi-tissue plant structure (PO:0025496) that is a petal-like, entire to digitately divided outgrowth from the outer margin of a nectary gland (PO:0009035) of a cyathium, as in Euphorbia.
reason: A real, diagnostic structure that every Euphorbia treatment uses (petaloid, digitate, patent, present or absent). PO has nothing narrower than nectary, and no pattern turns 'appendage of a gland' into a class. Propose to PO upstream together with a cyathium class.
